name: Catalyst-design quantum computer
subtitle: a quantum computer that finds cheap fertilizer catalysts

effects.effect: qubits in superposition can solve some problems, like factoring, exponentially faster
plants need nitrogen from the soil

effect: qubits in superposition can solve some problems, like factoring, exponentially faster
how: Making fertilizer eats one to two percent of the world's energy because the Haber process needs fierce heat and pressure, while soil bacteria do it at room temperature with an enzyme too complex for any ordinary computer to simulate. A quantum computer, whose qubits explore many arrangements of electrons at once, works out exactly how the enzyme's metal core breaks nitrogen apart, then screens man-made look-alikes for one that works in a farm-sized reactor.
obstacle: It needs around a million error-corrected qubits; today's machines have a few hundred noisy ones.
why: Simulating the nitrogen-fixing enzyme is a famous target; no quantum computer has done it.
real: FeMoco quantum simulation exists only as resource estimates and proposals (Reiher et al. 2016 onward); no quantum hardware has done it.
